name: Bistro Elba
signature: A beachy, artfully dilapidated French bistro on Ocean Beach Road, twice-baked soufflé, ocean-trout gravlax, and a wine list built on small emerging French producers.
editorNote:
Bistro Elba is the Sorrento room that makes you feel like you have found the real version of the village. The space is deliberately low-key, timber floors worn soft, candlelight, a short menu chalked up each day, and the cooking is classic French bistro done with enough restraint to feel entirely of its place. Twice-baked cheese soufflé, gin-cured ocean trout with cucumber and dill, whole flounder, duck leg slow-cooked properly. Nothing on the plate is trying to be clever.

The wine list is the other reason to come. It leans into small, emerging French producers, natural-adjacent, cleanly made, and priced so you are not punished for ordering a second bottle, and the team knows every label well enough to hand you something you have never heard of and trust you will love it.

Book for dinner on a Friday in autumn. Sit at the bar if the dining room is full. Order the soufflé twice. It is that kind of place.
whyWeGo: Sorrento has many restaurants that try to feel like a destination. Bistro Elba is the one that actually feels like somewhere.
ifOnlyOneThing: Book for dinner on a Friday in autumn, sit at the bar if the dining room is full, and order the soufflé twice.
